key_insight: Train a learned reward that measures visual equivalence between a model's rendered output and the target visual, enabling reinforcement learning to directly optimize visual fidelity for vision-to-code tasks.
problem_solved: Existing RL rewards for vision-to-code are misaligned: rule-based or coarse embedding similarities fail to capture fine-grained visual differences needed to reconstruct charts, tables, and SVGs accurately.
method: Learn a visual-equivalence reward model that scores how well a generated, rendered output matches the target visual at fine granularity.
Use the learned reward to fine-tune LVLMs with reinforcement learning (policy optimization), replacing coarse or handcrafted rewards.
Design the reward training to exploit rendered comparisons and dense visual features so small structural or styling errors are penalized appropriately.
impact: Provides a practical way to align RL objectives with visual fidelity, improving the correctness and usability of models that generate executable visual representations (e.g., chart/table/SVG code). This helps practitioners deploy LVLMs that produce visually accurate, runnable outputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → LVLM generates code → render → reward model compares render vs target → RL update loop
Before/after render pairs: examples showing improvements in chart/table/SVG fidelity
Reward model attention or heatmap over rendered pixels highlighting where mismatches are detected
Evaluation chart: fidelity metrics (visual score) comparing supervised fine-tuning vs Visual-ERM-enhanced RL
paper_title: Visual-ERM: Reward Modeling for Visual Equivalence
paper_authors: Ziyu Liu, Shengyuan Ding, Xinyu Fang, Xuanlang Dai, Penghui Yang
